trivial_change_silence.notes: Perfectly applicable. One-line enum .value bugfix was approved with zero substantive comments by all reviewers. Gemini bot confirmed correctness, fadara01 said 'LGTM', mgoin (maintainer) said 'Sorry about that, LGTM!'. No inline code comments at all. The skill correctly predicted that reviewers would approve without debate.

key_insight: Trivial one-line bugfixes with obvious correctness (enum .value access) and proper issue references are reliably fast-tracked. The trivial_change_silence skill is well-calibrated for this pattern.
hypothesis: N/A — prediction was fully correct. The trivial_change_silence skill accurately identified that a mechanical one-line bugfix with clear provenance (referenced both the bug issue and the introducing PR) would sail through review. The 0.95 confidence was appropriate; in hindsight 0.97+ would have been justified since there were truly zero substantive comments. One minor observation: mgoin's 'Sorry about that' suggests maintainers feel accountable when their changes introduce bugs, which may make them even more likely to fast-approve the fix — a social signal worth noting but not worth encoding as a skill.
